harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: LDAP is running persistently on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test. The staged alex and sam records retain their supplied identities and mail addresses. Node2 can find both users. Anonymous writes fail, while authenticated administrator updates succeed. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities.
actions_performed: Installed Xenial-compatible OpenLDAP 2.4.42 packages without changing the Ubuntu 16.04 release or 4.4 kernel.
Generated and stored the LDAP administrator credential in a root-only file on node1.
Imported the staged people OU and both user records; enabled slapd at boot.
Installed the LDAP client on node2 and verified remote searches.
Verified anonymous write rejection and a reversible authenticated administrator update.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, verifying changed boot IDs and recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: LDAP directory imported without changing supplied identities or mail addresses
evidence.summary: The staged LDIF and final directory both show alex/Alex North/alex@branch.test and sam/Sam West/sam@branch.test, with two total users.

evidence.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree and find both users
evidence.summary: Remote searches from node2 returned both complete user records before and after restarts.

evidence.requirement: Updates require an authenticated administrator and anonymous writes fail
evidence.summary: Anonymous modifications failed with authentication-required before and after restart; authenticated administrator modifications succeeded and test attributes were removed.

evidence.requirement: Operating-system release and kernel preserved with legacy-compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained Ubuntu 16.04 with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic; OpenLDAP 2.4.42 packages from Xenial were used.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart and LDAP recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID a9593011…, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 04a178c8…, and recovered slapd listener plus both records.

evidence.requirement: Node2 mandatory restart and client recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 35c87ec9…, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 67f39d73…, and recovered LDAP client access to both remote records.

attempts.summary: LDAP is running persistently on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test. The staged alex and sam records retain their supplied identities and mail addresses. Node2 can find both users. Anonymous writes fail, while authenticated administrator updates succeed. Both nodes were restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities.
